reason: Conversation 1 asked the key question the ground truth prioritises (which device trips, RCD vs MCB), explained how to identify it, laid out the genuinely open possibilities (hob leakage, moisture, RCD type, overload, loose connection) without overclaiming, and escalated properly to a registered electrician, tightening its advice once the smell emerged (minimise use, stop on any recurrence, electrician soon). Its one weakness is stopping short of a firm 'stop using' despite weekly trips plus a smell. Conversation 2 was safe but asserted an unsupported diagnosis from the outset ('most likely an earth leakage in the power module', later 'the boil-overs are very likely the cause', 'active earth fault'), never asked which switch trips, told the homeowner to 'unplug' a hardwired hob, and leaned on repetitive templated warnings rather than honest, proportionate guidance.
